1: ---
2: name: code-project-map-build-maintain
3: description: "You are a project cartography expert specializing in codebase mapping, dependency analysis, and knowledge preservation across AI agent sessions. Build a single structured project map once, then read it at the start of every session instead of rescanning the codebase. Maintain the map and a session log so that understanding of the project stays stable, token usage stays low, and no structural context is lost between sessions."
4: ---
5: 
6: ## 1. ROLE AND PURPOSE
7: 
8: You are an agent that maintains a single source of truth about the project structure in the file `.PROJECT_MAP.md`.
9: 
10: The purpose of this skill: to save you from re-analyzing the codebase in every new session. You build the project map once, and then read it instead of rescanning the entire project every time.
11: 
12: Why this matters:
13: - saves tokens and time;
14: - stable understanding of the project across sessions;
15: - control: you can see which sections are current and which are outdated;
16: - change history — in the session log.
17: 
18: A full project analysis is performed only once — at initialization, or upon an explicit user request. In all other cases, you work from the map.
19: 
20: ## 2. FILES
21: 
22: - `.PROJECT_MAP.md` — the project map. The single source of truth about the structure, modules, data flows, and conventions.
23: - `.SESSION_LOG.md` — the session log. History of map changes and open questions.
24: 
25: ## 3. SESSION START RULES (ALWAYS)
26: 
27: At the start of every session, before any work, perform the following in order:
28: 
29: 1. Read `.PROJECT_MAP.md`.
30: 2. Read the last 10 entries from `.SESSION_LOG.md`.
31: 3. If the files do not exist — perform the BUILD PROCEDURE (section 5), inform the user that the map has been created, and continue with the task.
32: 4. Do not scan the entire project if the map covers your task.
33: 5. If the task touches an area marked in the map as `stale` (outdated), read ONLY those files and update the corresponding sections of the map.
34: 6. If the map contradicts the actual code — see section 10 (Escalation).
35: 
36: ## 4. PRIORITY OF SOURCES OF TRUTH
37: 
38: If sources contradict each other, the priority is as follows:
39: 
40: 1. Explicit user instruction in the current session.
41: 2. `.PROJECT_MAP.md` (current version).
42: 3. Actual code — selectively, only in case of discrepancy or a `stale` mark.
43: 
44: ## 5. MAP BUILD PROCEDURE
45: 
46: Performed once at initialization or upon explicit request.
47: 
48: Analyze the project and create `.PROJECT_MAP.md` strictly according to the template in section 6. What to determine during analysis:
49: 
50: 1. Technology stack — from manifests: `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, `pom.xml`, `*.csproj`, `Gemfile`, `composer.json`, and similar.
51: 
52: 2. Entry points — `main.*`, `index.*`, `app.*`, `server.*`, `cmd/`, `bin/` folders, and similar.
53: 
54: 3. Run, test, and build commands — from `Makefile`, `scripts/`, CI configs, `README`, the scripts section of manifests.
55: 
56: 4. Significant modules — top-level folders and packages that contain real logic. Do not include small utility folders in the map.
57: 
58: 5. Dependency graph between modules — based on imports and references.
59: 
60: 6. Project conventions:
61:    - code style;
62:    - naming;
63:    - error handling;
64:    - logging;
65:    - configuration;
66:    - commit rules;
67:    - branching and PRs.
68: 
69: 7. External integrations — APIs, databases, queues, third-party services. For each, specify where the secrets are stored (file path or variable name), but WITHOUT the secret values themselves.
70: 
71: 8. Hot spots:
72:    - frequently changed files (based on `git log`);
73:    - the largest and riskiest modules.
74: 
75: Also create `.SESSION_LOG.md` with a single header line:
76: `# SESSION LOG`.
77: 
78: ## 6. TEMPLATE FOR THE .PROJECT_MAP.md FILE
79: 
80: Strictly follow this structure:
81: 
82: ```
83: # PROJECT MAP
84: 
85: > version: 1
86: > updated: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
87: > commit: <short-sha | n/a>
88: > agent: <model/name>
89: 
90: ## 1. Overview
91: 
92: - Purpose: <1–3 sentences>
93: - Stack: <language, frameworks, DB, key libraries>
94: - Entry point: <file:line>
95: - How to run: <command>
96: - How to test: <command>
97: - How to build: <command | n/a>
98: 
99: ## 2. Structure (significant paths only)
100: 
101: <root>/
102: ├── <dir>/   # purpose
103: ├── <dir>/   # purpose
104: └── <file>   # purpose
105: 
106: ## 3. Key modules
107: 
108: ### <path/module>
109: 
110: - Role: <what it does, why it is needed>
111: - Public API: <functions/classes/endpoints/events>
112: - Depends on: <modules>
113: - Depended on by: <modules>
114: - Files: <list>
115: - Notes / pitfalls: <...>
116: 
117: ### <path/module>
118: 
119: - ...
120: 
121: ## 4. Data flows and scenarios
122: 
123: - Scenario A (<name>): <module> -> <module> -> <module>
124: - Scenario B (<name>): ...
125: - Scenario C (<name>): ...
126: 
127: ## 5. Project conventions
128: 
129: - Code style: ...
130: - Naming: ...
131: - Error handling: ...
132: - Logging: ...
133: - Configuration: ...
134: - Commits: ...
135: - Branching / PR: ...
136: 
137: ## 6. External dependencies and integrations
138: 
139: | Integration | Type | Where used | Where config/secrets are (no values) |
140: |-------------|------|------------|--------------------------------------|
141: | <...>       | API  | <module>   | .env#KEY_NAME                        |
142: 
143: ## 7. Hot spots
144: 
145: - Frequently changed: <files>
146: - Riskiest: <files + why>
147: - stale: <section — what and why requires re-checking>
148: 
149: ## 8. Known limitations and TODO
150: 
151: - ...
152: ```
153: 
154: ## 7. UPDATING THE MAP
155: 
156: Update `.PROJECT_MAP.md` ONLY in these cases:
157: 
158: - the structure has changed: modules added, removed, or renamed;
159: - the public API of a module has changed;
160: - run, test, or build commands have changed;
161: - conventions or external integrations have changed;
162: - the user has explicitly asked for an update.
163: 
164: When updating, follow this order:
165: 
166: 1. Increase `version` by 1.
167: 2. Update the `updated` and `commit` fields.
168: 3. Do not rewrite sections that were not affected by the changes.
169: 4. Mark changed places with the marker `<!-- CHANGED vN -->`, where N is the new version.
170: 5. If a section is outdated but cannot be verified right now, mark it as `stale` and indicate the reason.
171: 
172: ## 8. SESSION LOG
173: 
174: At the end of each session, add an entry to `.SESSION_LOG.md`.
175: New entries are added on top, immediately after the `# SESSION LOG` header.
176: 
177: Entry format:
178: 
179: ```
180: ## YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM — <brief topic>
181: 
182: - Task: <what needed to be done>
183: - Touched: <files and modules>
184: - Map changes: <none | vN -> vN+1, list of sections>
185: - Open questions: <what remains unresolved>
186: ```
187: 
188: ## 9. PROHIBITIONS
189: 
190: - Do not scan the entire project "just in case."
191: - Do not duplicate file contents in the map — only cards, relationships, and roles.
192: - Do not update the map without reason: it is noise and wasted tokens.
193: - Do not store secrets, tokens, passwords, or keys in the map or log.
194: - Do not delete sections of the map — mark them as `stale` or `deprecated`.
195: 
196: ## 10. ESCALATION ON DISCREPANCY
197: 
198: If the map contradicts the actual code:
199: 
200: 1. Stop work on the affected module.
201: 2. Inform the user: which section of the map, what the discrepancy is, what you propose to fix.
202: 3. After confirmation — update the map and continue the task.
203: 
204: ## 11. QUICK REFERENCE
205: 
206: - Session start: I read PROJECT_MAP.md and SESSION_LOG.md, work from the map.
207: - No map: I build it according to the template, create the log, inform the user.
208: - Task touches stale: I read only those files, update the section.
209: - Changed structure or API: I update the map, version+1, add CHANGED vN.
210: - End of session: I write an entry in SESSION_LOG.md.

The terms **`entire enable`** and **`trails`** are core components of **Entire** (`entire.io`), a Git forge and collaboration platform designed for AI-driven coding agents (created by former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke)[1][2]. 

Here is what they mean and how they work according to the official documentation:

---

### 1. `entire enable` (CLI Setup)
`entire enable` is the primary command used to initialize and activate Entire inside a local Git repository[3][1]. 

* **What it does:** It configures your local environment, hooks into Git, and prepares the repository to automatically capture agent sessions, prompts, tool calls, and checkpoints whenever you or your coding agent (such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Pi) write and commit code[3][4][5].
* **Common Usage:**
  ```bash
  entire enable --agent claude-code
  ```
* **Key Flags:**
  * `--agent <NAME>`: Targets hooks for a specific coding agent (e.g., `claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor`, `pi`)[3].
  * `--checkpoint-remote <PROVIDER:OWNER/REPO>`: Configures an optional separate repository to push and store sensitive checkpoint/session data[3].
  * `--force` (`-f`): Reinstalls hooks by removing existing Entire hooks first[3].
  * If Entire was previously configured but disabled, running `entire enable` re-enables it[3].

---

### 2. Trails (Replaces Pull Requests for Agentic Coding)
**Trails** are Entire’s modern alternative to traditional Pull Requests, built specifically for workflows where AI agents write the majority of the implementation[6].

* **The Problem They Solve:** Standard PRs only show final code diffs (`what changed`), leaving reviewers in the dark about the agent's trial-and-error process, prompts, and reasoning (`why it changed`)[7]. Trails bundle the context behind a change alongside the code[6].
* **How Trails Work:**
  * **Creation:** A trail can start from a bug report/feature request on Entire, or directly via your agent before/after implementation[6]. Trails can also span across multiple repositories to group related changes together[6].
  * **Automated Agent Evaluations (Evals):** Every time code is pushed to a trail, Entire triggers independent cloud sandbox review agents[6]. These agents evaluate the commit and assign scores and rationales (e.g., looking at *Security*, *Slop*, or *Human Review Required*)[6].
  * **The Iteration Loop:** Evals display the current run alongside historical runs[6]. If a score is failing (e.g., an orange "slop" or security warning), developers instruct their coding agent to keep refining and pushing until the scores stabilize and turn green[6].
  * **Merging:** Unlike traditional PRs that rely heavily on quick human spot-checks, a Trail is designed to be merged only when confidence is high, risk is low, and all automated/human evaluation findings are cleared[6].

With no arguments, launches an interactive wizard: pick repos to mirror, pick one or more regions, then creates every (repo, region) mirror in parallel and prints the clone URLs. --cluster requires a <repo>.

With a <repo>, places it on every cluster named by --cluster — repeat the flag or comma-separate the hosts — in parallel, then waits for each to become usable. Pass --no-wait to return as soon as the placements are registered. Idempotent on (repo, cluster), so naming a cluster the repo is already on reports it rather than failing.

When --cluster is omitted, an interactive terminal offers the available clusters as a multi-select; non-interactive runs default to aws-us-east-2.entire.io.

With an /et/ ref, places replicas of an Entire-native repo and waits for each to be seeded. A native mirror goes in a region other than the repo's own, so only those clusters are offered and --cluster has no default there: non-interactive runs must name one.

Every cluster is attempted: one that fails does not stop the others, and the command exits non-zero naming the ones that did. A GitHub mirror whose initial clone is still running when --timeout passes is reported as still syncing, not as a failure: the clone carries on in the background, and `entire repo view <repo>` shows when it lands.

Repository references name their forge: /gh/<owner>/<repo> for a GitHub mirror, /et/<project>/<repo> for an Entire-native repository.

Adds a git remote so fetch and push go through Entire instead of the forge.

The repo is resolved from the current clone's remotes; pass [repo] to name a different one. With more than one cluster to choose from, a terminal gets a picker and a script gets the repo's own cluster — --cluster selects one either way, the same as `entire repo clone`.

<remote-name> must not already exist: as with `git remote add`, an occupied name is refused rather than repointed. --override repoints it instead, printing the URL it replaced — the only record of it, and with any credentials redacted, so keep the original yourself if you need it.

It only ever edits local git config — the cluster must already serve the repo (`entire repo mirror add`); nothing server-side is changed.

Repository references name their forge: /gh/<owner>/<repo> for a GitHub mirror, /et/<project>/<repo> for an Entire-native repository.

Usage:
  entire repo remote add <remote-name> [repo] [flags]

Examples:
  entire repo remote add entire
  entire repo remote add entire --cluster aws-us-east-2.entire.io
  entire repo remote add entire /gh/octocat/hello-world
  entire repo remote add origin --override

Flags:
      --cluster string          Cluster host to use when the repo is on several

      --override[=true|false]   Repoint <remote-name> when it already exists instead of refusing

12: - You MUST request a screenshot as part of your initial `get_design_context` call—use that render of the design as the visual target that the rendered implementation MUST visually match.
13: - IF no screenshot is returned by `get_design_context`, you MUST call `get_screenshot` directly before editing.
14: - IF `get_design_context` flags a response as sparse, you CANNOT use it directly for implementation; you MUST correlate its hierarchical child node IDs with the screenshot, then request the visible child nodes in one parallel batch of `get_design_context` calls to obtain high-fidelity responses.
15: - You MUST implement exclusively from the high-fidelity `get_design_context` responses; the design screenshot is the visual target, NEVER use it in code as an implementation asset.

18: 
19: - You MUST adapt returned code to the project's stack and conventions and inspect likely project paths BEFORE editing; treat returned code as a high visual fidelity non-interactive prototype - translate raw absolute positioning into project-native layout unless the design can only be represented with fixed positioning; identify which portions of the design are intended to be interactive and implement the design as interactive code.
20: - You MUST inspect likely project paths AND installed design library dependencies for code components, assets, and tokens which match the design BEFORE editing. You MUST reuse or compose suitable matches instead of recreating them with raw markup, inline styles or hardcoded values; modify or supplement them ONLY when they cannot accurately express the design.
21: - You MUST apply Code Connect precisely at its mapped node(s), ALWAYS directly reuse the connected component UNLESS it cannot be configured or extended to express the design. Styling or wiring effort is NOT an exception.
22: - You MUST use each visible static asset—image or SVG—in the EXACT position(s) used in the design, substituting only for EXACT matches found in the codebase/design library when one exists. NEVER omit, edit, redraw, extract paths from, inline, substitute, or incorrectly use an asset—but keep API-, prop-, or data-supplied imagery dynamic. ALL provided SVGs have root width and height attributes which you MUST NOT override when changing wrapper styles; avoid broad 100% × 100% sizing.
23: - You MUST ensure ALL static assets used have been downloaded as described in the `get_design_context` response leaving NO references to temporary Figma asset URLs in code. DO NOT use other tools to download assets unless explicitly told to do so. Inspect only metadata/root dimensions when necessary, avoid reading asset byte sequences unless the task explicitly requires doing so.

2: name: figma-spec
3: description: "This skill is required to create, read, edit, review, or comment on Figma specs. You must read it when working on a PRD, brief, RFC or any kind of document in either a standalone Figma spec or a Figma spec embedded in a Figma Design or Figjam file."
4: disable-model-invocation: false
5: ---
6: 
7: # Work with a Figma spec
8: 
9: Check that `figma.spec` is defined in your first `use_figma` script; it exists only when the file’s plan has Specs enabled. If it is undefined, explain that Specs is not enabled for this file’s plan and stop the workflow. To create a new standalone Figma spec file, call `whoami` to choose a destination plan, then call `create_new_file` with `editorType: "figspec"` and that plan's `key` as `planKey`. If it reports that Figma Specs is not available on that plan, offer the user's other plans or stop.
10: 
11: A native Figma spec is GitHub-Flavored Markdown (GFM) under a `SPEC_BLOCK` node. A standalone Figma spec is just one spec; a FigJam or Design file can contain several embedded specs.
12: 
13: ## Discover and choose the Figma spec
14: 
15: Resolve a supplied URL `node-id` when present with `figma.getNodeByIdAsync` and require `type === "SPEC_BLOCK"` plus `specBlockType === "DOCUMENT"`. Otherwise, search the current page with `findAllWithCriteria({ types: ['SPEC_BLOCK'] })`, filtering for `specBlockType === "DOCUMENT"` (and examine content with `figma.spec.getContent` if needed) until you find your target. If it's not on the current page, load other pages one at a time with `page.loadAsync()` and repeat your query, stopping once the target is resolved.
16: 
17: Pass the resolved root ID to every content call. Omit `specNodeId` only when the file is known to contain exactly one Figma spec; omission throws otherwise. Never edit ordinary canvas text nodes as a fallback.
18: 
19: ## Create a Figma spec on a canvas
20: 
21: ```js
22: // Creates an embedded Figma spec on a Design or FigJam canvas (not a standalone Figma spec file).
23: const { specNodeId } = await figma.spec.createOnCanvasAsync({
24:   title: 'Untitled spec',
25:   content: '# Title\n\nA paragraph.\n',
26: })
27: 
28: const specNode = await figma.getNodeByIdAsync(specNodeId)
29: if (!specNode) throw new Error('The created Figma spec could not be resolved')
30: 
31: const after = await figma.spec.getContent({ specNodeId })
32: if (!after.markdown.includes('A paragraph.')) {
33:   throw new Error('The new Figma spec content was not applied')
34: }
35: ```
36: 
37: Always pass a non-empty `title` and a `content` string (`''` is allowed). `title` names the root; include any desired `# H1` in `content`.
38: 
39: ## Content methods
40: 
41: ```js
42: // READ — returns specNodeId, markdown, title, etc.
43: // The body is `markdown`, not `content`.
44: const before = await figma.spec.getContent({ specNodeId: chosenSpec.id })
45: const page = await figma.spec.getContent({
46:   specNodeId: before.specNodeId,
47:   offset: 100,
48:   maxLines: 50,
49: })
50: 
51: // REPLACE — clears + recreates the document; use only for an empty first draft.
52: await figma.spec.setContent({
53:   specNodeId: before.specNodeId,
54:   content: '# Title\n\nA paragraph.\n',
55: })
56: 
57: // EDIT — find/replace; each oldText must match exactly once.
58: await figma.spec.editContent({
59:   specNodeId: before.specNodeId,
60:   edits: [{ oldText: 'First paragraph.', newText: 'Edited first paragraph.' }],
61: })
62: 
63: const after = await figma.spec.getContent({ specNodeId: before.specNodeId })
64: if (!after.markdown.includes('Edited first paragraph.')) {
65:   throw new Error('The targeted Figma spec edit was not applied')
66: }
67: ```
68: 
69: - Use **`getContent`** with the same `specNodeId` before edits and to verify writes; DON'T rely on screenshots.
70: - Default to multiplayer-safe, surgical **`editContent`**.
71: - Use destructive **`setContent`** only for an empty first draft or an explicit whole-document replacement.
72: 
73: ## Critical rules
74: 
75: 1. **`editContent` requires exactly one match.** Zero or multiple `oldText` matches fail without changes. Add surrounding context to make it unique.
76: 2. **Pass Markdown as plain strings.** Never encode it with `Buffer`/base64 or decode it with `atob()`. Base64 is only for image data URLs inside Markdown.
77: 3. **Keep Markdown and traversal separate.** `figma.spec.*` handles content; node traversal exposes only document roots and embedded-canvas branches.
78: 4. **Preserve comment markers.** Keep overlapping `[comment:<uuid>]…[/comment:<uuid>]` pairs unchanged around the same text, or the thread may detach or disappear. When in doubt copy the marked span exactly and edit around it.
79: 5. **Use portable references.** Shared Figma specs must use links such as GitHub permalinks, never machine-local paths or `localhost` URLs.
80: 
81: ## Style
82: 
83: - Keep the title block first and formatted as H1, even when its text is empty. Never remove it or insert blocks before it.
84: - Prefer bold text in table header row.
85: - Use `<ins>` for underline, including combined formatting: `<ins>**bold and underlined**</ins>`. Do not use `<u>`, which only works in HTML imports.
86: 
87: ## Images
88: 
89: Images use GFM image syntax inside `setContent` or `editContent`:
90: 
91: - `![alt](data:image/png;base64,...)` embeds bytes that are decoded and uploaded.
92: - `![alt](https://host/img.png)` is fetched server-side; disallowed hosts are rejected.
93: 
94: `getContent` emits image URLs as `https://<host>/spec/<fileKey>/image/<sha>?w=<width>&h=<height>`.
95: 
96: ## Comments
97: 
98: Use `figma.spec.comments.*` for anchored threads. Prefer comments over leaving silent edits when you're unsure of a change.
99: 
100: ```js
101: const comment = await figma.spec.comments.create({
102:   specNodeId: before.specNodeId,
103:   anchorText: 'the exact rendered text to anchor to', // MUST appear exactly once
104:   contextText: 'a longer unique substring containing anchorText', // optional; disambiguates repeats
105:   message: 'Comment body (markdown).',
106: })
107: 
108: const { root, replies, hasMore } = await figma.spec.comments.getThread({ uuid: comment.uuid })
109: await figma.spec.comments.reply({ uuid: comment.uuid, message: 'A reply.' })
110: ```
111: 
112: - `anchorText` must match exactly once in the rendered Figma spec. Use a longer `contextText` containing it to disambiguate repeated text.
113: - `getThread` and `reply` require the root comment UUID surfaced by a `[comment:<uuid>]` marker; never pass a reply UUID to `reply`.

6: # use_figma — Figma Plugin API Skill
7: Use the `use_figma` tool to execute JavaScript in Figma files via the Plugin API. All detailed reference docs live in `references/`.
8: 
9: When available, call `create_session` with `fileKey` and `description` before file reads or edits (create the file first if needed), then pass the returned `sessionId` unchanged to every call that accepts it, including follow-ups and work across files.
10: 
11: **Always include `figma-use` in the comma-separated `skillNames` parameter when calling `use_figma`. If this skill was loaded via an MCP resource, you MUST prefix the name with `resource:` (e.g. `resource:figma-use`).** This is a logging parameter used to track skill usage — it does not affect execution.
12: 
13: **If Figma MCP tools appear as deferred tools, batch-load all their schemas in a single `ToolSearch` call** using the `select:` syntax — e.g. `ToolSearch query="select:use_figma,get_screenshot,get_metadata,create_new_file"`. One round trip beats six.
14: 
15: **MANDATORY for visible design changes:** Before the first mutating `use_figma` call, load [figma-generate-design](../figma-generate-design/SKILL.md) alongside this skill and include both names in every mutating call’s `skillNames`. This applies from a single visible property or element to a full page, screen, or composed multi-section view—even when the user calls that view a component. `figma-use` provides the Plugin API rules; `figma-generate-design` provides design-system discovery through `search_design_system`, asset importing, and incremental assembly.

17: **Reusable library exception:** If the primary deliverable is a reusable component, component set, variant system, variable/token collection, style foundation, or other library asset intended for reuse or publication, load [figma-generate-library](../figma-generate-library/SKILL.md) instead. It provides the component-creation workflow—variable foundations, variant sets, and design-token bindings—that `figma-use` alone does not cover. For tasks that include both library assets and a composed design that uses them, load both companion skills. Read-only `use_figma` calls need neither.
18: 
19: **3D transforms:** For perspective, depth, X/Y tilt, isometric cubes, or other static 3D poses, load [figma-3d-transforms](../figma-3d-transforms/SKILL.md) when available. It owns the gated `transform3d`, `scene3d`, and `transformOrigin` API guidance, including fields that may be absent from the general typings. Follow this skill's node-creation rules, then apply the 3D poses to the resulting nodes. If the 3D skill or APIs are unavailable, explain that 3D authoring is not enabled in this session. Flat in-plane rotation uses `node.rotation` and does not need the 3D skill.

21: For other APIs, load [plugin-api-standalone.index.md](references/plugin-api-standalone.index.md) to understand what is possible. When you are asked to write plugin API code, use this context to grep [plugin-api-standalone.d.ts](references/plugin-api-standalone.d.ts) for relevant types, methods, and properties. This is the definitive source of truth for the general API surface. It is a large typings file, so do not load it all at once, grep for relevant sections as needed.
22: 
23: IMPORTANT: Whenever you work with design systems, start with [working-with-design-systems/wwds.md](references/working-with-design-systems/wwds.md) to understand the key concepts, processes, and guidelines for working with design systems in Figma. Then load the more specific references for components, variables, text styles, and effect styles as needed.
24: 
25: ## 1. Critical Rules
26: 1.  **Use `return` to send data back.** The return value is JSON-serialized automatically (objects, arrays, strings, numbers). Do NOT call `figma.closePlugin()` or wrap code in an async IIFE — this is handled for you.
27: 2.  **Write plain JavaScript with top-level `await` and `return`.** Code is automatically wrapped in an async context. Do NOT wrap in `(async () => { ... })()`.
28: 3.  `figma.notify()` **throws "not implemented"** — never use it
29: 3a. **Return node IDs and keep workflow state outside the Figma file.** Set human-readable component purpose and usage in `node.description` only on a `COMPONENT` or `COMPONENT_SET` — never on a frame or instance.
30: 3b. **Narrow before accessing type-specific properties.** Check `node.type`, use a capability guard such as `"characters" in node`, or prefilter with `findAllWithCriteria`. `characters` requires a text-capable node; optional chaining does not protect unsupported property access.
31: 4.  `console.log()` is NOT returned — use `return` for output
32: 5.  **Size construction calls for safe retry and validate from evidence.** Do not split a working operation solely to create validation checkpoints. Batch related work when the resulting script remains safe to retry; a complete section or page may be built in one call. Split when crossing page context, when partial execution would be difficult to recover, or after an actual failure requires a targeted retry. Return affected IDs and relevant counts, names, or bounds from each write—this counts as structural validation. Run a separate structural check only when required evidence is missing or after a relevant mutation. Normally take one screenshot after composition and one after a visual fix. The most recent passing screenshot is the final check; do not repeat it when nothing relevant changed. Stop once requirements pass.
33: 6.  Colors are **0–1 range** (not 0–255): `{r: 1, g: 0, b: 0}` = red. Paint `color` objects use `{r, g, b}` **only — no `a` field**; opacity goes at the paint level (`{ type: 'SOLID', color: {...}, opacity: 0.5 }`).
34: 7.  Fills/strokes are **read-only arrays** — clone, modify, reassign
35: 8.  **Every text edit follows the canonical recipe: load font → `await` → mutate → return affected node IDs.** Skipping the load throws `Cannot write to node with unloaded font "<family> <style>"`. The rule covers more than `characters` — it applies to any operation on nodes with unloaded fonts (`appendChild`, `insertChild`, `setBoundVariable`, `setExplicitVariableModeForCollection`, `setValueForMode`, `findAll` callbacks touching text). When mutating existing text, load the node's *current* fonts via `getStyledTextSegments(['fontName'])`, not a hardcoded default. Inter is preloaded in most environments so other families surface this bug more often — the recipe is the same for every font. Use `await figma.listAvailableFontsAsync()` first if the style string is unverified — **never guess** (`"SemiBold"` vs `"Semi Bold"` is a common footgun). For `FONT_FAMILY`-scoped variables, load every value across every relevant mode before `setBoundVariable("fontFamily", …)`, `setValueForMode`, or `setExplicitVariableModeForCollection`. `lineHeight`/`letterSpacing` take `{unit, value}`, not bare numbers. See [Canonical text-edit recipe](references/gotchas.md#canonical-text-edit-recipe-font-load--await--mutate--return-ids).
36: 9.  **Pages load incrementally** — use `await figma.setCurrentPageAsync(page)` to switch pages and load their content. The sync setter `figma.currentPage = page` does **NOT** work and throws `"Setting figma.currentPage is not supported"`. Page context resets to the **first page** at the start of every `use_figma` call, so re-switch each call; switch **at most once per call** and fan multi-page work out in parallel — see [Page Rules](#2-page-rules-critical) and [gotchas.md](references/gotchas.md#set-current-page-once-per-use_figma-call--split-multi-page-work-into-parallel-calls).
37: 10. `setBoundVariableForPaint` returns a **NEW** paint — must capture and reassign
38: 11. `createVariable` accepts collection **object or ID string** (object preferred)
39: 12. **`layoutSizingHorizontal/Vertical` is value-restricted by structural context — `FIXED` always works, `HUG` and `FILL` do not.** `'HUG'` is valid only on an auto-layout frame itself OR on a **TEXT** child of one. `'FILL'` is valid only on a child of an auto-layout frame that is also not absolute-positioned, not inside an immutable frame, and not a canvas-grid child. Practical consequence: append to an auto-layout parent FIRST, then set `HUG`/`FILL` — a newly-created or unparented node can't satisfy the rule yet. The property itself exists on every `SceneNode`; the error is value-rejection, not "no such property". See [Gotchas](references/gotchas.md#layoutsizinghorizontallayoutsizingvertical-value-rules-fixed-hug-fill).
40: 12a. **Use auto-layout for containers that hold related children.** When children have a structural relationship — stacked, side-by-side, aligned, gapped, hugged — wrap them in `figma.createAutoLayout()`, not `figma.createFrame()` with absolute `x`/`y`. Absolute coordinates govern where a container sits on the canvas; auto-layout governs how its children relate inside it. Skipping the container leaves no protection against text reflow, content changes, or overlap.
41: 12b. **`layoutSizing*` and `*AxisSizingMode` are different enums — don't cross them.** `layoutSizingHorizontal`/`layoutSizingVertical` (set on a **child**) take `'FIXED'|'HUG'|'FILL'`; `primaryAxisSizingMode`/`counterAxisSizingMode` (set on the **frame** itself) take `'FIXED'|'AUTO'`. So `layoutSizingVertical = 'AUTO'` is invalid (use `'HUG'`), and `counterAxisSizingMode = 'FILL'` throws `Expected 'FIXED' | 'AUTO', received 'FILL'` (use `'FIXED'`/`'AUTO'`). Two more errors from the same setter — `Error: in set_layoutSizingHorizontal: node must be an auto-layout frame or a child of an auto-layout frame` and `Error: in set_layoutSizingHorizontal: FILL can only be set on children of auto-layout frames` — mean the node isn't in an auto-layout context yet; **recommendation: make the parent auto-layout (`figma.createAutoLayout()`) and `appendChild` the node before setting** (see Rule 12). See [Gotchas](references/gotchas.md#layoutsizing-vs-axissizingmode-two-different-sizing-enums).
42: 12c. **`resize()` resets sizing modes to `FIXED`, so call it BEFORE setting `layoutSizing*`.** A wrapping **TEXT** block needs `textAutoResize = 'HEIGHT'` plus an explicit FIXED width (`resize()`), NOT `FILL` alone — the default `WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT` mode ignores `FILL` and collapses the node to a near-zero-width thread. Verify `node.width > 0` afterward.
43: 13. **Position new top-level nodes away from (0,0).** Nodes appended directly to the page default to (0,0). Scan `figma.currentPage.children` to find a clear position (e.g., to the right of the rightmost node). This only applies to page-level nodes — nodes nested inside other frames or auto-layout containers are positioned by their parent. See [Gotchas](references/gotchas.md).

Реализовать русскоязычный сайт кастомного Telegram-клиента exDesktop. Он знакомит с продуктом,направляет к загрузке,показывает команду установки,отвечает на вопросы и связывает с сообществом. ### 8.3. Точное содержание

#### 01. Начало работы

**Что такое exDesktop?**

> Модифицированный кросс-платформенный клиент для Windows, Linux и macOS на основе исходного кода Telegram.
> Material Design Expressive, глубокая кастомизация, функции приватности, настройки визуала, режим стримера, функционал exteraGram, AyuGram и других клиентов сообщества, адаптированный под Desktop.

**Это официальный клиент Telegram?**

> Нет. exDesktop — независимый проект сообщества, не связанный с Telegram FZ-LLC.

#### 02. Установка и обновления

**Какие системы поддерживаются?**

> Windows, Linux и macOS. Для Windows доступны установщик и portable-архив,
> для Linux — tar.gz, для macOS на Apple Silicon — dmg или zip.

**Как установить и обновить клиент?**

> На Linux и macOS используй команду с главной страницы. На Windows скачай
> установщик из GitHub Releases. В клиенте предусмотрены автоматические обновления.

#### 03. Возможности и плагины

**Что можно настроить?**

> Оформление, иконки, сообщения, уведомления и элементы интерфейса.
> Есть режим стримера, функции AyuGram и дополнительные настройки приватности.

**Как начать разрабатывать плагины?**

> Начни с документации PythonSDK. Поддержка форматов .plugin, .elyx и .eaf
> ещё дорабатывается — учитывай ограничения совместимости.

#### 04. Сообщество и развитие

**Где следить за изменениями?**

> Новости — в Telegram-канале, список изменений — в Changelog.
> Исходный код и опубликованные версии доступны на GitHub.

**Как сообщить об ошибке или предложить идею?**

> Создай GitHub Issue: укажи версию клиента, систему и шаги воспроизведения.
> Задать вопрос и обсудить идею можно в Telegram Chat.

## 11. Темы, движение и состояния

### 11.1. Переключение темы

Одна структура для каждой страницы с переключением цветовых ролей, а не независимые копии содержимого. Размеры, тексты, изображение и маска совпадают. Общие шапка, подвал, ссылки и повторяющийся ответ — единые.

При первом открытии использовать сохранённый выбор; если его нет — системное предпочтение; если оно недоступно — тёмную тему. Сохранять выбор между страницами и посещениями. Переключение не меняет текущий адрес/якорь и не сбрасывает позицию чтения. Устранить мигание светлым фоном при запуске тёмной темы.

Смена фона, текста и контуров плавная, около 250ms. Размеры при переключении не анимировать, контент не должен прыгать. Правила сохранения и системного выбора дополняют статические макеты.

### 11.2. Вращение

Вращается **внешняя sunny-обводка**, а изображение аватара и подпись неподвижны, как в референсе. Sunny и фоновый flower: один оборот по часовой стрелке за 40s, линейно, вокруг собственного центра. Clover: против часовой стрелки, один оборот за 28s. В макете записан один оборот; на сайте повторять бесконечно без рывка на стыке.

Не вращать всю карточку hero, персонажа или подпись. Центры: sunny 174/174 внутри области 348×348; flower 155/155; clover 65/65. Анимация не изменяет размеры и не сдвигает поток.

При системном запросе уменьшения движения отключить непрерывное вращение и плавную прокрутку. Сохранить статичную композицию и все действия. Не допускать нагрузки, из-за которой прокрутка идёт рывками; ненужное движение в скрытой вкладке приостанавливать.

### 11.3. Состояния — дополнительные требования

- Hover: слой цвета содержимого с прозрачностью 8%, без скачка размеров.
- Pressed: слой 12%, без изменения текста и высоты.
- Keyboard focus: заметный внешний акцентный контур 2px с отступом 2–3px, не срезанный родителем.
- Disabled использовать только при реальной недоступности действия. В базовом сайте таких элементов нет: не выключать загрузку и ссылки произвольно.
- Наведение и нажатие: 150–250ms. Переход к якорю: около 350ms с плавным ускорением/замедлением; пользователь может отменить его обычной прокруткой.
- Нет обязательных загрузочных экранов: сайт отображается без ожидания API. Если позже подключено получение версии, ошибка запроса не скрывает сайт и не ломает Releases; остаётся настроенное значение версии.
- Возврат браузером должен восстанавливать ожидаемую страницу и позицию чтения.

## 13. Доступность, семантика и качество

Один главный заголовок на страницу: exDesktop или «Ответы. Без лишнего.». Далее логичная иерархия разделов/вопросов. Шапка, навигация, основная часть, статьи и подвал размечены по назначению. Ссылки остаются ссылками, переключение темы — кнопкой. Поддержать Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter; Space для кнопок. Фокус видимый, порядок чтения естественный.

Аватар: альтернативное описание «Аватар METAWKA, разработчика exDesktop». Декоративные фигуры и дублирующие текст иконки скрыты от средств чтения. У темы доступное название действия: «Включить светлую тему» / «Включить тёмную тему». Текущая страница и раздел оглавления программно отмечены. Зона нажатия минимум 44×44; у визуальной вкладки высотой 40 можно расширить область, не перекрывая соседей.

Контраст обычного текста не ниже 4.5:1, крупного 3:1. Текст выделяется, масштабирование не запрещено. Команда — отдельная моноширинная область. Ссылки различимы не только цветом: формой области, иконкой и фокусом.

Язык страницы русский. Заголовок вкладки главной «exDesktop — кастомный клиент Telegram», FAQ «FAQ — exDesktop». Описание главной взять из актуального hero. Favicon — существующий знак. Предпросмотр при распространении ссылки без выдуманных рейтингов, загрузок и релизов.

Аватар имеет заранее заданные пропорции и не сдвигает контент при загрузке. Векторы и шрифты оптимизировать без потери кириллицы и формы. Важный портрет первого экрана не откладывать до прокрутки. Не превращать сайт целиком в одну картинку.

## 14. Переиспользование и ограничения

Единые сущности: шапка, тема, pill-ссылка, подвал, декоративные формы, данные FAQ, список внешних адресов и команда установки. Ответ «Что такое exDesktop?» одинаковый в кратком и полном FAQ; типографика отличается по макету. Общие изменения должны попадать на обе страницы и в обе темы.

Не возвращать удалённое владельцем: список «Windows / Linux / macOS» внизу hero, подпись «Сделано с любовью к деталям», подзаголовок под «Есть вопросы? Есть ответы.», подпись под заголовком подвала. Не подменять новое описание ранним и не сокращать развёрнутый ответ.

Не добавлять обещаний безопасности, новых платформ, статистики и неподтверждённых функций. Реальные скриншоты, информация и Roadmap теперь включены в согласованный объём. Не требуются установка клиента из браузера, выполнение команды, переписка внутри сайта, собственная страница SDK, вход и серверная обработка форм.

import os, re

icon_dir = 'public/assets/icons'
for f in os.listdir(icon_dir):
    if not f.endswith('.svg'):

    path = os.path.join(icon_dir, f)
    with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as file:
        content = file.read()
    
    # replace stroke=\"#...\" with stroke=\"currentColor\"
    content = re.sub(r'stroke=\"#[0-9a-fA-F]+\"', 'stroke=\"currentColor\"', content)
    # replace fill=\"#...\" with fill=\"currentColor\" if not fill=\"none\"

    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as file:
        file.write(content)

print('Updated icons to currentColor')

> version: 3

## 1. Overview <!-- CHANGED v3 -->

- Purpose: Official website for the exDesktop project with Material Design 3 Expressive theme, responsive layout, full FAQ and external integrations.
- Stack: TypeScript, JavaScript, React 18, Vite 5, CSS Custom Properties (Theme tokens)
- Entry point: src/main.tsx:1 (HTML entry: index.html:1)
- How to run: npm run dev
- How to test: n/a
- How to build: npm run build

## 2. Structure (significant paths only) <!-- CHANGED v3 -->

exDesktop website/
├── public/                 # Static assets, icons, screenshots, avatar
│   ├── assets/             # Vector marks, sunny frame, decorative flower/clover
│   │   └── icons/          # 21 functional SVG icons extracted from Figma
│   ├── screenshots/        # Real client preview screenshots (settings, appearance)
│   └── avatar.jpg          # Developer avatar (460x460)
├── src/                    # React + TypeScript source code
│   ├── components/         # Modular UI components
│   │   ├── Header.tsx      # Adaptive navigation header (desktop capsule + mobile burger)
│   │   ├── MobileMenu.tsx  # Modal slide-down navigation panel with keyboard trap
│   │   ├── Hero.tsx        # Hero with rotating sunny/flower/clover, avatar cookie mask, CTAs
│   │   ├── VisualPreview.tsx # Screenshots gallery with external links
│   │   ├── Features.tsx    # Appearance, Privacy, Plugins cards
│   │   ├── Installation.tsx # Terminal command with copy button + GitHub repo card
│   │   ├── Roadmap.tsx     # 3 development stages with source links
│   │   ├── QuickFaq.tsx    # Home preview FAQ with direct anchors

│   │   └── Icon.tsx        # Dynamic SVG mask-based icon component
│   ├── data/

│   ├── styles/
│   │   ├── variables.css   # MD3 Expressive theme tokens (Dark & Light)
│   │   └── global.css      # Typography, reset, focus rings, keyframe animations
│   ├── App.tsx             # Theme toggle, client-side routing, view orchestration
│   ├── main.tsx            # React DOM client bootstrap
│   └── types.ts            # TypeScript data models
├── index.html              # HTML5 entry with complete SEO, Open Graph & Twitter meta tags
├── vite.config.ts          # Vite bundler configuration
├── tsconfig.json           # TypeScript configuration
├── package.json            # Project dependencies and npm scripts
├── .gitignore              # Ignored files (cartography, logs, node_modules, dist)
└── README.md               # Project description

## 3. Key modules <!-- CHANGED v3 -->

### App (src/App.tsx)
- Role: App root, manages theme state ('dark' | 'light'), HTML5 history navigation, dynamic title
- Public API: React component <App />
- Depends on: components/*, styles/*
- Files: src/App.tsx, src/main.tsx

### Header & MobileMenu (src/components/Header.tsx, MobileMenu.tsx)
- Role: Top navigation bar for desktop/tablet/mobile, theme switcher, responsive burger menu
- Public API: <Header />, <MobileMenu />
- Files: src/components/Header.tsx, src/components/MobileMenu.tsx

### Hero (src/components/Hero.tsx)
- Role: Top showcase card, rotating sunny SVG, flower, clover, developer avatar in cookie mask
- Files: src/components/Hero.tsx

### Installation & Repository (src/components/Installation.tsx)
- Role: Interactive terminal card for Linux/macOS curl command + GitHub repository card
- Files: src/components/Installation.tsx

### FAQ (src/components/QuickFaq.tsx, FullFaq.tsx)
- Role: Quick FAQ preview on home page and dedicated Full FAQ page with 4 categories, TOC, community support card
- Files: src/components/QuickFaq.tsx, src/components/FullFaq.tsx, src/data/siteData.ts

## 4. Data flows and scenarios <!-- CHANGED v3 -->

- Scenario A (Theme Switch): User clicks sun/moon -> App toggles state -> data-theme on html updates -> CSS variables smoothly transition (250ms)

- Scenario C (Command Copy): User clicks terminal box -> clipboard API copies install command -> visual feedback ('Скопировано!')

- Code style: Modern React functional components, hooks, strict TypeScript
- Naming: PascalCase for components, camelCase for functions/vars, kebab-case for CSS/files

- Frequently changed: src/data/siteData.ts, src/styles/variables.css
- Riskiest: none
- stale: none

# PROJECT MAP

> version: 4
> updated: 2026-11-18 14:35
> commit: pending
> agent: Antigravity IDE Agent

## 1. Overview <!-- CHANGED v4 -->

- Purpose: Official website for the exDesktop project with Material Design 3 Expressive theme, responsive layout, full 16-section FAQ/docs (formats, emulation, Xposed hooks, web windows, PluginGuard, DevServer, Elyx, crossplatform), and external integrations.
- Stack: TypeScript, JavaScript, React 18, Vite 5, CSS Custom Properties (Theme tokens)
- Entry point: src/main.tsx:1 (HTML entry: index.html:1)
- How to run: npm run dev
- How to test: n/a
- How to build: npm run build

## 2. Structure (significant paths only) <!-- CHANGED v4 -->

exDesktop website/
├── public/                 # Static assets, icons, screenshots, avatar
│   ├── assets/             # Vector marks, sunny frame, decorative flower/clover
│   │   └── icons/          # 21 functional SVG icons extracted from Figma
│   ├── screenshots/        # Real client preview screenshots (settings, appearance)
│   └── avatar.jpg          # Developer avatar (460x460)
├── src/                    # React + TypeScript source code
│   ├── components/         # Modular UI components
│   │   ├── Header.tsx      # Adaptive navigation header (desktop capsule + mobile burger)
│   │   ├── MobileMenu.tsx  # Modal slide-down navigation panel with keyboard trap
│   │   ├── Hero.tsx        # Hero with rotating sunny/flower/clover, avatar cookie mask, CTAs
│   │   ├── VisualPreview.tsx # Screenshots gallery with external links
│   │   ├── Features.tsx    # Appearance, Privacy, Plugins cards
│   │   ├── Installation.tsx # Terminal command with copy button + GitHub repo card
│   │   ├── Roadmap.tsx     # 3 development stages with source links
│   │   ├── QuickFaq.tsx    # Home preview FAQ with direct anchors
│   │   ├── FullFaq.tsx     # Full FAQ & Docs page with sticky TOC, 16 categories, code blocks, tables & lists
│   │   ├── Footer.tsx      # 6 pill links (Telegram, Chat, Changelog, Contact, GitHub, PluginSDK)
│   │   └── Icon.tsx        # Dynamic SVG mask-based icon component
│   ├── data/
│   │   └── siteData.ts     # Site links, copy, roadmap items, rich FAQ & documentation entries
│   ├── styles/
│   │   ├── variables.css   # MD3 Expressive theme tokens (Dark & Light)
│   │   └── global.css      # Typography, reset, focus rings, keyframe animations
│   ├── App.tsx             # Theme toggle, client-side routing, view orchestration
│   ├── main.tsx            # React DOM client bootstrap
│   └── types.ts            # TypeScript data models (FaqCategory, FaqItem, FaqTable, etc.)
├── index.html              # HTML5 entry with complete SEO, Open Graph & Twitter meta tags
├── vite.config.ts          # Vite bundler configuration
├── tsconfig.json           # TypeScript configuration
├── package.json            # Project dependencies and npm scripts
├── .gitignore              # Ignored files (cartography, logs, node_modules, dist)
└── README.md               # Project description

## 3. Key modules <!-- CHANGED v4 -->

### App (src/App.tsx)
- Role: App root, manages theme state ('dark' | 'light'), HTML5 history navigation, dynamic title
- Public API: React component <App />
- Depends on: components/*, styles/*
- Files: src/App.tsx, src/main.tsx

### Header & MobileMenu (src/components/Header.tsx, MobileMenu.tsx)
- Role: Top navigation bar for desktop/tablet/mobile, theme switcher, responsive burger menu
- Public API: <Header />, <MobileMenu />
- Files: src/components/Header.tsx, src/components/MobileMenu.tsx

### Hero (src/components/Hero.tsx)
- Role: Top showcase card, rotating sunny SVG, flower, clover, developer avatar in cookie mask
- Files: src/components/Hero.tsx

### Installation & Repository (src/components/Installation.tsx)
- Role: Interactive terminal card for Linux/macOS curl command + GitHub repository card
- Files: src/components/Installation.tsx

### FAQ & Documentation (src/components/QuickFaq.tsx, FullFaq.tsx) <!-- CHANGED v4 -->
- Role: Quick FAQ preview on home page and dedicated Full FAQ/Docs page with 16 categories from exdesktop.xyz/docs/ and GitHub README, sticky TOC, syntax-highlighted code blocks, tables and bullet lists
- Files: src/components/QuickFaq.tsx, src/components/FullFaq.tsx, src/data/siteData.ts

### Footer (src/components/Footer.tsx) <!-- CHANGED v4 -->
- Role: Bottom navigation pills with PluginSDK link, copyright and legal disclaimer
- Files: src/components/Footer.tsx

## 4. Data flows and scenarios

- Scenario A (Theme Switch): User clicks sun/moon -> App toggles state -> data-theme on html updates -> CSS variables smoothly transition (250ms)
- Scenario B (Navigation & Anchors): User clicks FAQ / links -> pushState -> scrollIntoView smoothly navigates to section without full reload
- Scenario C (Command Copy): User clicks terminal box -> clipboard API copies install command -> visual feedback ('Скопировано!')

## 5. Project conventions

- Code style: Modern React functional components, hooks, strict TypeScript
- Naming: PascalCase for components, camelCase for functions/vars, kebab-case for CSS/files
- Styling: Pure CSS Custom Properties, Material Design 3 Expressive color roles
- Commits: Conventional commits
- Branching / PR: Trails / main

## 6. External dependencies and integrations

| Integration | Type | Where used | Where config/secrets are (no values) |
|-------------|------|------------|--------------------------------------|
| GitHub      | Forge| Git origin | secret-tool / git-credential-libsecret|
| Entire      | Agent Platform | Hooks, Remotes & Trails | .entire/ / Secret Service |
| Telegram    | Community & Channels | Links & Chat buttons | src/data/siteData.ts |

## 7. Hot spots

- Frequently changed: src/data/siteData.ts, src/components/FullFaq.tsx
- Riskiest: none
- stale: none

## 8. Known limitations and TODO

- Build passes cleanly with zero errors (TypeScript + Vite)
- Deploy static build to hosting or GitHub Pages when requested
